unmapped_findings: The present as-hot-rolled low-density steel has a specific yield strength (SYS) of 73.1 MPa g^-1 cm^3 and specific ultimate tensile strength (SUTS) of 97.7 MPa g^-1 cm^3, owing to its low density.
Specific modulus (E/ρ) of the present steel is calculated to be 32.7 GPa g^-1 cm^3, remarkably higher than the typical ~25 GPa g^-1 cm^3 for light metals such as aluminum, magnesium, and titanium.

The present steel achieves a strength-ductility balance (SYS × UE value around 9-10 MPa g^-1 cm^3) positioned among existing ceramic-reinforcement steels while maintaining a high specific modulus (~32.7 GPa g^-1 cm^3, highest among the compared steels).

δ-ferrite contributes ~170 MPa (over 30 % of the overall yield strength) as a stable strengthening baseline, nearly constant throughout deformation, while the strengthening contribution from austenite increases with strain (Fig. 12(c)); the phase stress of δ-ferrite surpasses that of austenite by nearly 50 % in the elastic stage.
FEM-simulated phase stresses at ~830 MPa global true stress: TiB2 reaches ~1180 MPa (highest), δ-ferrite ~710 MPa, austenite ~670 MPa (lowest, softest phase).

Onset of yielding of the present steel (global true stress ~490 MPa, close to the measured σy) is attributed to plastic flow of austenite (micro-yielding), not δ-ferrite; above ~600 MPa both matrix phases flow plastically and TiB2 continues to bear increasing load via strain hardening of the matrix.

Damage evolution: first defect-containing particle fracture occurred at true plastic strain εp = 0.0069 and applied true stress σa = 556 MPa (exceeding σ0.2 = 503 MPa); cracks oriented nearly perpendicular to the tensile axis. Statistical analysis of 336 TiB particles (189 predominantly austenite-contacting, 147 ferrite-contacting) showed austenite-surrounded particles exhibited significantly higher fracture frequencies; particle fracture accelerates final failure more than particle decohesion.
Large particles (>10 μm) constitute >80 % of the volume fraction of TiB2 and dictate bulk mechanical behavior; small particles (0.8-5.0 μm) account for only 1.01 % of the volume fraction.
Fracture surface shows a mixed fracture mode comprising ductile dimples, quasi-cleavage fracture of TiB2 particles, and particle/matrix decohesion.

Austenite grains with GOS < 2° (fully recrystallized) account for 90.8 % (area fraction) of the austenite phase, while recrystallized δ-ferrite accounts for only 52.2 % of the ferrite phase, showing sluggish δ-ferrite recrystallization during hot rolling.
Average thickness of ferrite bands is 4.3 μm, smaller than that of austenite layers (12.1 μm).
